verses.text: If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you, and he gives you a sign or a wonder,
and the sign or the wonder comes to pass, of which he spoke to you, saying, “Let us go after other gods” (which you have not known) “and let us serve them”;

you shall not listen to the words of that prophet, or to that dreamer of dreams; for Yahweh your God is testing you, to know whether you love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
You shall walk after Yahweh your God, fear him, keep his commandments, and obey his voice, and you shall serve him, and cling to him.

That prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death, because he has spoken rebellion against Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, to draw you aside out of the way which Yahweh your God commanded you to walk in. So you shall remove the evil from among you.

If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son, or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend, who is as your own soul, entices you secretly, saying, “Let us go and serve other gods,” which you have not known, you, nor your fathers;
of the gods of the peoples who are around you, near to you, or far off from you, from the one end of the earth even to the other end of the earth;
you shall not consent to him, nor listen to him; neither shall your eye pity him, neither shall you spare, neither shall you conceal him;
but you shall surely kill him. Your hand shall be first on him to put him to death, and afterwards the hands of all the people.
You shall stone him to death with stones, because he has sought to draw you away from Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
All Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall not do any more wickedness like this among you.
If you shall hear about one of your cities, which Yahweh your God gives you to dwell there, that
certain base fellows have gone out from among you, and have drawn away the inhabitants of their city, saying, “Let us go and serve other gods,” which you have not known;
then you shall inquire, and make search, and ask diligently. Behold, if it is true, and the thing certain, that such abomination was done among you,
you shall surely strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, destroying it utterly, with all that is therein and its livestock, with the edge of the sword.

You shall gather all its plunder into the middle of its street, and shall burn with fire the city, and all every bit of its plunder, to Yahweh your God. It shall be a heap forever. It shall not be built again.

Nothing of the devoted thing shall cling to your hand, that Yahweh may turn from the fierceness of his anger, and show you mercy, and have compassion on you, and multiply you, as he has sworn to your fathers;
when you listen to Yahweh your God’s voice, to keep all his commandments which I command you today, to do that which is right in Yahweh your God’s eyes.

footnotes.content: A prophet's credentials don't rest on crowds or charisma alone. The Lord warns Israel: discernment is your calling, not blind allegiance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A miracle can seduce the heart if the heart is unanchored. Even signs come and go, but the Lord's covenant stands. That makes all the difference.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The test itself is Yahweh's gift—a trial of love rather than punishment. In this verse, I hear Jesus in the garden, praying for his disciples to hold fast to the Father when seduction and fear both press in.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Walking after the Lord, fearing Him, keeping His commands—these are the marks of a people who belong to Him. Clinging to His voice is the truest safety there is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophet speaks "rebellion" when they lead away from the Redeemer who brought Israel out of bondage. To forget deliverance is to lose your bearings entirely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seduction often comes from the people closest to us—family, beloved friends. That closeness is what makes the temptation bite so hard, and why discernment must begin in the heart before it reaches the ear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The gods of the surrounding nations—whether near or distant—all make the same promise: you will become like gods if you bow to them. But becoming is not freedom; it is slavery in a prettier mask.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not to consent, not to listen, not to pity—these are stern mercies. Mercy to the community sometimes looks like firmness toward what would scatter the fold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The hand raised first is a sign of a covenant people acting together—not in vengeance, but in preservation of the God who called them. Your neighbor's faith is woven into your own salvation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The one who draws you away from Yahweh draws you back toward Egypt—toward the very bondage from which He already ransomed you. The Lord's jealousy here is the jealousy of a rescuer guarding His rescued.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fear falls on all Israel when they see the seriousness with which their God guards the covenant. This fear is not terror; it is the awe of a people who know they are treasured and held.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cities too can be tempted to stray. A community's life together can become a place where rebellion is quietly chosen, one voice and one hand at a time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Base fellows"—worthlessness is what it looks like when people separate themselves from the God who names them. They carry a hollow echo, and they draw others into that hollowness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Inquire, search, ask diligently—Israel is called to discernment, not gossip or haste. Wisdom takes time. In this patient asking, I see how the Spirit still works: truth tested and revealed, never rushed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The complete destruction—the burning away—is a radical mercy: it seals off the wound before corruption can spread. It is harsh medicine for a people in covenant with a God who cannot be divided.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The plunder heaped in the street, the city burned—nothing for personal gain, all consumed as witness. What is devoted to the Lord must not cling to our hands for profit or pride.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let nothing cling to your hand—not the spoils of rebellion, not the comfort of compromise. When we release what is not ours to keep, the Lord's mercy and compassion fall on us like rain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo here: the voice of covenant love that still calls us to listen, to keep, to do what is right in His eyes. The command is old, but the offer—mercy poured out—is always new.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
